report_name: Ransomware Gangs Qilin and Barracuda Claim New Corporate Victims

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: A prolific ransomware group that claimed responsibility for an attack against the U.S.-based company Danser. The group operates a dark web leak site to pressure victims using double extortion tactics.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

threat_actors.name: Barracuda
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed an attack on the Turkish manufacturing firm EVINOKS. The group threatened to release stolen data for free on its dark web leak site to pressure the victim.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The core activity of the Qilin and Barracuda ransomware groups, involving the encryption of victim files to disrupt operations and demand a ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Both Qilin and Barracuda ransomware groups exfiltrate sensitive data from their victims before encryption, a tactic known as double extortion, to increase pressure for ransom payment.

malware.name: Qilin Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload deployed by the Qilin group to encrypt files on the victim's network. The article links to the Malpedia entry for this malware.

malware.name: Barracuda Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload deployed by the Barracuda group to encrypt files and steal data from the victim's network.

identities.name: Danser
identities.description: A U.S.-based company claimed as a victim by the Qilin ransomware group.

identities.name: EVINOKS
identities.description: A Turkish manufacturer of hotel and restaurant equipment breached by the Barracuda ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: Qilin Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web leak site operated by the Qilin ransomware group to name victims and publish stolen data as part of their double extortion strategy.

infrastructure.name: Barracuda Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web leak site operated by the Barracuda ransomware group to name victims and threaten the release of stolen data.

indicators.name: Ransomware Behavior - VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 1b9d6b8e-4a3c-4b8e-8f9a-1b9d6b8e4a3c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common precursor to ransomware deployment to prevent easy file restoration.
references:
  - https://www.hookphish.com/blog/ransomware-group-qilin-hits-danser/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-01
tags:
  - attack.t1490
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a common ransomware technique of deleting volume shadow copies to hinder system recovery, as suggested in the article's hunting hints.

indicators.name: Defense Evasion - Encoded PowerShell Command
indicators.pattern:
title: Encoded PowerShell Command Execution
id: 2c8e7c9f-5b4d-4c9f-9a0b-2c8e7c9f5b4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of encoded PowerShell commands, a common technique for defense evasion and lateral movement by threat actors like ransomware groups.
references:
  - https://www.hookphish.com/blog/ransomware-group-qilin-hits-danser/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-01
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1027
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -enc '
      - ' -encodedcommand '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of encoded PowerShell commands, a common defense evasion technique suggested as a hunting hint for ransomware activity.

references:
